label: Software engineering — general, mid-level
notes: v2, 2026-08-22: rubric pass after log 7.36. Every criterion is now stated as the
CONCRETE question that measured reliably, and carries the evidence for it.
The finding that drove this: the same concept scores very differently depending on
whether it is asked concretely or abstractly. `ownership` as an extraction enum
(i / we / unclear) measured 15/18; `ownership` as a rubric quality measured 16%.
`impact` as a quality measured 28-65% and unstable; `has_result` -- did they state an
outcome -- measured 10/10. The model reports concrete textual facts reliably and
abstract qualities unreliably, in every encoding tried (log 7.30-7.36).
So a criterion is scored only if it has a named source and a measured reliability.
Anything else is shown to the user or dropped. A score the system cannot evidence is
the 'plausible but wrong' failure that plan section 15 rates most damaging.
REMOVED: `communication` -- a meta-judgement about an answer, not a fact in it.
NOT SCORED: `technical_depth` and `structure` -- no concrete proxy has been measured.
NOT SCORED: `weighs_options` -- 14/20, too weak to score, worth showing.
The DESIGN phase is deliberately unscored: a hypothetical design answer has no
situation, action or outcome, and nothing else currently observable applies to it.
Scoring it on criteria that do not fit is worse than not scoring it.
answer_shape is REQUIRED and validated at load -- plan 3.2, never defaulted.

technical_depth.measured: 44% as an abstract quality (log 7.36); no concrete proxy measured

questions: To start — tell me a bit about yourself and what you're working on at the moment.
What drew you to this role in particular?
Tell me about a time you disagreed with a technical decision on your team.
Describe a production incident you were responsible for resolving.
Tell me about something you shipped that didn't work out the way you expected.
Tell me about a time you had to learn an unfamiliar codebase quickly.
Walk me through a performance or scalability problem you've hit. What did you measure, and what did you change?
Tell me about a schema or data-model change you've made to a system that was already live.
Describe how you decide a change is ready to ship. Use a recent example.
Tell me about a technical decision you made that you'd make differently now.
Walk me through how you'd design a rate limiter for a public API. Take a minute first if you want.
phases.scored_false_reason: Observed but NOT scored. The four parts extract cleanly -- every quote is real text -- but scoring them inverts the ranking: the weakest of four measured answers scored 4/5, above two of the three strong ones (log 9.6). The criteria reward MENTIONING a topic, and 'I don't know how you'd stop that' is indistinguishable from anticipating a failure when both are quotes. Section 7.10 measured `mentions_tradeoff` at 7/10 and called it a genuine judgement call; quoting does not rescue it, because the judgement is in what counts as meeting the criterion, not in finding the text. The report DESCRIBES the design answer instead.
phases.probe_budget_reason: Lowered from 3 in log 9.10. It was raised when the design question drew ZERO probes because a fluent answer read as complete; `design-gap->probe` now guarantees one follow-up deterministically. The adaptive stop does NOT apply here -- a hypothetical has no situation, action or result -- so this budget is the only pacing the question has, and at 3 plus pool it ran to 5 follow-ups and became the longest question in the session, spending reserve the scored phases could have used.

questions: Tell me about a time you gave difficult feedback to a colleague.
